+# LiteLLM #34399 review
+
+## Decision
+
+Provider backoff takes precedence over router failover when the failed response contains `Retry-After`. `Router._time_to_sleep_before_retry` extracts response headers before deciding whether a healthy sibling permits an immediate retry. A healthy sibling still returns zero when no upstream backoff applies.
+
+The change is intentionally limited to the existing `Retry-After` contract. Existing `_calculate_retry_after` bounds, jitter, and router `retry_after` behavior are unchanged.
+
+## Regression coverage
+
+The mapped router test constructs two deployments with the same `api_base`, representing a shared rate-limited upstream. With deterministic jitter, `Retry-After: 42` produces 42 seconds while the sibling is healthy; omitting the header produces zero and preserves immediate failover. The existing local router retry expectation is aligned with this precedence.
+

arguments.summary: For LiteLLM Router retries, an explicit provider Retry-After takes precedence over immediate sibling-deployment failover because deployments may share one upstream quota. Extract error response headers before the healthy-deployment fast path; if Retry-After is present, use the existing _calculate_retry_after policy. If no upstream Retry-After applies and another deployment is healthy, return zero to preserve immediate failover. Validate with two deployments sharing api_base, deterministic jitter, an explicit-header case that waits, and a header-absent case that returns zero. Re-index implementation, mapped regression tests, compatibility tests, and the review before promotion.
